Reuters: Over $600M in Stolen Binance Funds Flowed Through THORChain, Potentially Including Repeated Transfers; Another $342M Moved via CoinJoin According to Reuters, citing blockchain analytics firms including Chainalysis and Elliptic, North Korean hackers are moving crypto stolen in the Binance hack through THORChain and CoinJoin services. The firms estimate that over $600 million in stolen funds has flowed through THORChain, potentially including funds counted multiple times, while approximately $342 million has been moved through CoinJoin. TRM Labs estimates THORChain earned up to $1 million in fees from the related swaps. The Binance hack resulted in approximately $6.3 billion in stolen crypto assets, of which around $2.85 billion has been frozen by token issuers. Researchers say the laundering activity could continue for months or even years. — link

BNB Chain Releases New L1 Litepaper Targeting High-Frequency Trading, Payments, Private Finance, and Autonomous AI Agents BNB Chain released a new L1 litepaper targeting high-frequency trading, payments, private finance, and autonomous AI agents. It will run alongside BNB Smart Chain, retaining BNB as its native token without issuing a new one. The EVM-compatible L1 separates transaction ordering and execution, uses SubBlocks for preliminary ordering feedback, and reserves block capacity for payments and other designated transactions. Native account abstraction supports passkeys, transaction batching, revocable permissions, and gas sponsorship. Private settlement supports BNB and eligible BEP-20 tokens, alongside partially public application interactions. A public testnet is in development, parallel EVM execution is planned, and TEE-based ordering protection remains a proposal. — link

Highlight Clip: Brian Armstrong: Hackers Tried to Extort Coinbase, Only to Face a Bounty Hunt Brian Armstrong: Hackers Tried to Extort Coinbase, Only to Face a Bounty Hunt On November 25, 2026, Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said in an interview with WOLF Financial that companies must assume employees could be exposed to malware attacks and incorporate this risk into their security systems from the outset. As hackers increasingly use AI to launch attacks, defenders must also leverage AI to strengthen their security capabilities. Coinbase has deployed dedicated AI agents for cybersecurity to review every line of code before it goes live. Discussing the previous extortion attempt against Coinbase, Armstrong said the company chose not to give in to the hackers, instead publicly responding and offering a bounty for information that could help identify and apprehend the attackers, while cooperating with law enforcement to hold them accountable. — link
